html:
A Javanese noblewoman whose letters, written in Dutch, argued for girls' education and against forced marriage. Indonesia honours her as a pioneer of women's rights.

Kartini was born in Jepara, on the north coast of Java, in the Dutch East Indies. Her father was the regent. She went to a Dutch primary school, but at 12 she had to leave and stay at home until marriage, as custom demanded of noble daughters.

She read widely and wrote long letters to Dutch friends about the limits placed on Javanese women, polygamy and the gap between rulers and people. In 1903 she married the regent of Rembang, who let her open a small school for girls. She died in 1904, days after giving birth, at the age of 25.

In 1911 a Dutch official published her letters as Door Duisternis tot Licht, "Out of Darkness to Light". They fit the Dutch Ethical Policy of the time and inspired schools named after her. In 1964 Sukarno made her a national hero, and her birthday, 21 April, is Kartini Day.
